claims.claim: Pooled over three leaderboards the sealed final nRMSE is 0.562 and skill against column-mean imputation is 0.434.
Per-seed pooled skills of the sealed evaluation are 0.433, 0.427 and 0.433 (seeds 201-203), 157.4/160.6/161.0 s per seed.
Per-leaderboard nRMSE: MTEB 0.703, HELM Lite 0.501, Open LLM Leaderboard 0.482.

MTEB nRMSE at k=2,5,10,20 is 0.787, 0.722, 0.664, 0.638; per-added-benchmark reductions about 0.022, 0.012, 0.003 are differences of these values divided by added benchmarks; k=20 is about 7% of 297 columns.

Skill against greedy-forward ridge is 0.099 and against random-k ridge is 0.016; difference 0.083; implied error ratio about 1.09 is indicative only. Selector and imputer are scored jointly, so these margins are not a test of selection alone; the 0.016 margin is small and unresolved.
The sealed final evaluation completed with outcome qualified.

Sealed evaluation used seeds 201-203 with 14 episodes per seed. The identity of the sealed-evaluated source tree is not established by retained artifacts (presumably the development-selected pair or its latent-skill extension, which have identical development scores); no hash-comparison artifact exists.
Development-partition scores: simple pair 0.220, proposed pair 0.247 (seed scores 0.243 and 0.251), latent-extended pair 0.247 identical.

Development-partition nRMSE (1.067 vs 1.028), skill vs random-k (0.100 vs 0.132) and permuted gap (0.522 vs 0.568) are read from search-split metric files (analysis/search_metrics.json) rather than from the final registry.
Three configurations were scored in total on the development partition.
Final aggregate nRMSE of 0.562 is the equal-weight mean of the three leaderboard values; the valid-run flag requires real episodes to beat controls.
Benchmark suites: MMLU, BIG-bench, HELM, MTEB.
Item-level reduction of evaluation cost, adaptive item selection under an item-response model, and sparse benchmark distillation from several benchmarks.
Agreement analyses across benchmarks and low-dimensional capability models bear on how related benchmark scores are.
Latent-capability and scaling views of multi-benchmark performance; IRT; latent-factor predictors not run as baselines.
EM for Gaussian missing data, missingness assumptions, matrix completion, experimental design and submodular greedy selection, stacking and ridge are standard tools.
Open LLM Leaderboard component benchmarks: IFEval, BBH, MATH, GPQA, MuSR, MMLU-Pro.
